band_rationale: Normal = five hundred or more bills a year (the 2024-2025 volume, legislatures reacting at their own speed); fast = under two hundred, legislatures standing aside. Between is emerging.
counterevidence: A single tracker's classification; introduced bills are cheap signals; the enacted count is the one that binds.

crosswalk.note: Adaptation inside adopting organisations and sectors: regulated devices, state bills, call-centre uplift, reported executive impact.

definition: Count of state bills in NCSL's artificial-intelligence legislation tracker for the legislative year, with the enacted subset alongside.

evidence.snippet: the Transparency Coalition has found that 84 new AI-related laws have been passed and/or enacted across 27 states so far in 2026.
evidence.summary: Transparency Coalition: 84 new AI-related laws passed or enacted in 27 states in 2026 by 21 July, a count of laws rather than bills.

evidence.snippet: As of March 2026, state lawmakers in 45 states have already introduced 1,561 AI-related bills
evidence.summary: MultiState: 1,561 AI-related bills introduced in 45 states by March 2026, a count for the session so far rather than the full year.

name: US state AI bills introduced (legislative year)

status_events.author: evaluate
status_events.reason: NCSL's 2025 legislation tracker holds 1,035 state AI bills, of which 170 carry an enacted or signed status, counted from the published table on 11 Sep 2026. Inside the normal band (500 or more a year: legislatures reacting at their own pace). One tracker, scraped, tier 6, so the status is capped at emerging until a second count (MultiState or the Transparency Coalition) corroborates. Initial seed.

timing_rationale: Lagging: bills follow public attention to deployments already under way, and counts settle after the legislative year.
tracker_interpretation: Counted from NCSL's table, so scraped and pending until a human merges; bills are not laws.
why_it_matters: The institutional response the paper expects to lag deployment; volume says attention, enactments say binding rules.
